tasks.title: Pin exit codes with guard test
tasks.acceptance:
- internal/cli/exit.go declares the five codes of the §11.2 table: 0 success, 1 validation failure, 2 usage error, 3 file/configuration/external-command failure, 4 state conflict including lock timeout and partial post.
- A guard test asserts each numeric value literally, so a renumbering fails the suite rather than silently shipping.
- The codes are exported constants; no command uses a bare integer literal.
tasks.closed_reason:
- internal/cli/exit.go declares all five §11.2 codes: ExitOK 0, ExitValidation 1, ExitUsage 2, ExitFile 3, ExitState 4, each carrying the meaning the table gives it, under a comment pinning them to the spec.
- TestExitCodesArePinned in internal/cli/root_test.go asserts each of the five numeric values literally, so a renumbering fails the suite rather than shipping silently; verified by go test ./... .
- All five are exported package-level constants in package cli, reachable by every command.
- No command uses a bare integer exit literal: Execute() maps its error path onto ExitUsage, and a grep over cmd/ and internal/ finds no numeric argument to os.Exit. Gate: go test ./... ok, golangci-lint 0 issues.

tasks.title: Build the cobra root command
tasks.acceptance:
- A spf13/cobra root command named cr exists at cmd/cr with internal/cli holding the command tree.
- Record ids are PR-scoped, so every command that names one takes the pull request as an argument.
- go build ./cmd/cr produces a working binary that prints help with no arguments.
tasks.closed_reason:
- The spf13/cobra root command named cr was already in place from commit 243a344 and is verified intact rather than rewritten: cmd/cr/main.go is a three-line entry point calling cli.Execute(), and internal/cli/root.go holds the tree, the five §11.1 global flags, and the error-to-exit-code mapping onto ExitUsage.
- Record ids are PR-scoped, so internal/cli/pr.go adds the fence every such command will build on: parsePR rejects anything that is not a positive pull request number, prArgs(n) validates the arity and the leading pull request argument, and TestRecordIDCommandsTakeThePullRequest walks the whole command tree and fails any command whose Use names <record-id> without <pr> ahead of it, or that takes a <pr> without validating it. Both halves were proven to bite by temporarily registering violating commands and observing the failures, then reverted.
- go build ./cmd/cr produces a working binary that prints help with no arguments. The root previously emitted only its Short line, because cobra suppresses the usage block for a command that is neither runnable nor populated, so newRootCmd now sets Args cobra.NoArgs and a RunE returning cmd.Help(). The freshly built /tmp/cr-dev/cr run with no arguments prints the usage block and all five global flags and exits 0, while cr bogus exits 2, and TestRootPrintsHelpWithNoArguments pins the behaviour.
Out of scope: registering the §11 command rows belongs to the next task, command-surface-stubs, so the tree-walk guard passes vacuously today and becomes load-bearing the moment those stubs land.

tasks.title: Register every specified command stub
tasks.acceptance:
- Every row of the §11 command table is registered with its documented argument shape and flags: init (--eject-roles), brief, review (--axis), claims record, merge (-o --repo --pr), record, map record, claims set-aside (--note), cells record, sandbox create|destroy, test (--filter), probe run (--kind), draft, post (--confirm --reconcile), answer, note (--remove), context, waivers list|remove (--repo --pr), stats (--repo), rules list (--dead --repo)|check|suggest, status, config (--resolved).

tasks.title: Exit two on usage errors
tasks.acceptance:
- A missing required argument, an unknown flag, or an unparseable pull request reference exits 2 per §11.2.
- Cobra's own usage errors are mapped to 2 rather than to cobra's default 1.
- Tested for at least three commands taking different argument shapes.

tasks.title: Switch JSON output by TTY
tasks.acceptance:
- Output is JSON when stdout is not a terminal or when --json is given, and human-readable coloured text otherwise, per §12.1.
- The decision is made once in a shared writer, not per command.
- Tested by driving a command with a pipe and with a pseudo-terminal.

tasks.title: Pretty-print JSON with empty slice rule
tasks.acceptance:
- JSON output is pretty-printed with two-space indentation per §12.2.
- Every slice field serialises as [] and never as null per §12.3; a test walks a fully-zero-valued payload of every output struct and asserts no null array appears.
- Constructors use make([]T, 0) rather than var x []T wherever a slice reaches output.

tasks.title: Attach hint to every error
tasks.acceptance:
- Every error carries a hint field naming the next actionable step per §12.4.
- A shared error type makes the hint a required construction parameter, so an error without one cannot be built.
- A test asserts that every error returned by the command tree carries a non-empty hint.

tasks.title: Implement compact flag omissions
tasks.acceptance:
- --compact omits output_tail, input, and ingested thread bodies per §12.5.
- --compact MUST NOT omit evidence or citations: the agent composes every posted body from them, so a compacted payload would leave the composition unfounded.
- Tested against a payload carrying all five fields.

tasks.title: Report posted boolean on write commands
tasks.acceptance:
- Every command that could have performed a network write reports a posted boolean per §12.6, so a dry run is distinguishable from a successful post in JSON as well as in a terminal.
- A dry-run cr post reports "posted": false; a confirmed one reports true.
- Commands that can never write omit the field rather than reporting false.

tasks.title: Wire the five global flags
tasks.acceptance:
- --json, --compact, --quiet, --no-color, and --repo <owner/repo> are registered as persistent flags with the effects of the §11.1 table.
- --repo overrides repository detection rather than supplementing it.
- Each flag is exercised by a test on at least one command.

tasks.title: Exempt honesty disclosures from quiet
tasks.acceptance:
- --quiet suppresses informational messages but never an honesty disclosure. The seven exemptions of §11.1 are always printed: the disabled and unavailable axes of §4.5.4, the probe cap of §5.6.4, the forcing counts of §6.3.2, the waiver and duplicate counts of §10.1.6, the sandbox recreation notice of §5.1.6, the stale-round report of §9.3.2, and the comment cap of §1.6.2.
- The exemption is enforced by routing disclosures through a dedicated writer that ignores --quiet, not by remembering to check a flag at each call site.
- A test runs each of the seven situations under --quiet and asserts the disclosure still appears.
- §11.1's always-printed list is 'every lens of §4.5.4 that did not run', matching §8.4.3, §10.1.3, and §10.2 verbatim.

tasks.title: Implement the six-step text normalisation
tasks.acceptance:
- normalise() applies exactly the six steps of §1.4 in order: decode UTF-8, replace CRLF and lone CR with LF, strip trailing SPACE/TAB per line, collapse every run of SPACE/TAB anywhere in a line including leading indentation to one SPACE, drop leading and trailing blank lines while collapsing interior blank runs to one, and rejoin with single LF with no trailing LF.
- A one-line input normalises to that line with no terminator.
- Invalid UTF-8 fails with exit code 1.
- Normalisation does not case-fold, does not strip punctuation, and does not reorder lines; a test asserts each negative.

tasks.title: Compute truncated normalised SHA-256 hash
tasks.acceptance:
- A normalised hash is SHA-256 over the normalised text, lowercase hex, truncated to the first 16 characters, per §1.4.
- Every hash in the system routes through this one function; a test asserts a known input maps to a fixed 16-character value.
- The function is the sole hashing entry point, so §3.4.6, §7.4.1, §8.3.3, §9.2 and §6.1 cannot drift apart.

tasks.title: Close the axis id set
tasks.acceptance:
- A shared validator accepts exactly intent, correctness, convention, and test, per §1.5.
- Any other value in a profile, role, or rule axis field aborts the command with exit code 3 naming the offending file and value.
- The axis set is closed in v0.1; no configuration layer can extend it.
tasks.closed_reason:
- internal/axis/axis.go holds the one shared validator of §1.5, where ids is the literal set intent, correctness, convention, test, Valid and Validate read only that literal, and TestValidateAcceptsExactlyTheFourAxisIDs asserts both the exact set IDs() returns and that Validate accepts every member.
- Any other value returns an *axis.InvalidError carrying the file, the field, and the offending value in its message, and exitCodeFor in internal/cli/exit.go maps that error, through any wrapping, onto ExitFile so Execute aborts with exit code 3, covered by TestValidateNamesTheOffendingFileAndValue and TestInvalidAxisExitsWithTheFileCode.
- The set is closed in v0.1 because the ids literal has no registration entry point and IDs() hands out a copy, which the tamper check in TestNoConfigurationLayerCanExtendTheAxisSet asserts by writing to the returned slice and finding the validator unchanged.
- No configuration layer can extend it, and the same test proves it by resolving a global config file and a CR_ variable that each name a fifth axis, then asserting no resolved setting addresses an axis id and that Validate still rejects the name.

Out of scope: the profile, role, and rule schemas that will call axis.Validate are later tasks, so no schema loader or call site was added here.

tasks.title: Create the global state directory tree
tasks.acceptance:
- cr init creates ~/.cr with every path of the §2.2 table: config.json, profiles/, roles/, rules/, repos/<owner>/<repo>/{config.json,roles/,rules/,triage.ndjson,rule-stats.ndjson}, state/<owner>/<repo>/pr-<n>/, context/<ISSUE-KEY>.ndjson, waivers/<owner>/<repo>.ndjson, and locks/.
- Paths are derived from one layout function so no command hand-builds a path.
- Running cr init twice is idempotent.
tasks.closed_reason:
- cr init creates the §2.2 tree: internal/state/layout.go names every path of the table and Init() creates the global ones (root, config.json, profiles/, roles/, rules/, repos/, state/, context/, waivers/, locks/), while EnsureRepo, EnsurePR, and EnsureContext create the placeholder-bearing paths (repos/<owner>/<repo>/{config.json,roles/,rules/,triage.ndjson,rule-stats.ndjson}, state/<owner>/<repo>/pr-<n>/, waivers/<owner>/<repo>.ndjson, context/<ISSUE-KEY>.ndjson) once a command knows the owner, repository, pull request, or issue key; TestInitCreatesTheGlobalTree and TestEnsureCreatesTheScopedPaths assert each one exists on disk, and the built binary was run against CR_HOME to confirm the real tree.
- Paths are derived from one layout function: the state.Layout type joins every path against a single injectable root resolved by Default() from CR_HOME or <home>/.cr, cr init calls only Layout methods, and TestLayoutDerivesEveryStatePath pins all 25 derived paths against the §2.2 table so no command needs to hand-build one.
- Running cr init twice is idempotent: directories go through os.MkdirAll and files through touchFile, which leaves an existing file byte-identical, verified by TestInitIsIdempotent writing a config and re-running Init, by the repeated EnsurePR assertion in TestEnsureCreatesTheScopedPaths, and by invoking the binary's init twice.
Out of scope: internal/cli/root.go still maps every command error onto ExitUsage, so a file failure from cr init exits 2 rather than the §11.2 ExitFile 3; correcting that belongs to usage-errors-exit-two.

tasks.title: Guard against writes inside the repository
tasks.acceptance:
- cr never writes inside the repository under review, with the single exception of git worktree registration metadata under .git/worktrees/ created by §5.1.
- cr never modifies the repository's tracked files, index, HEAD, stash, or any branch.
- A guard test runs a representative command sequence against a fixture repository and asserts git status is byte-identical before and after, apart from the permitted worktree registration.

tasks.title: Take advisory locks on writes
tasks.acceptance:
- Every write to per-PR state takes an exclusive advisory file lock via gofrs/flock, per §2.3.1.
- Reads are lock-free per §2.3.2.
- A concurrency test shows two writers serialising and a reader proceeding while a writer holds the lock.
tasks.closed_reason:
- Every write to per-PR state goes through the exclusive gofrs/flock lock of §2.3.1: internal/state/lock.go makes Write a method on the held *Lock rather than on the Layout, so no writer can reach a file under state/<owner>/<repo>/pr-<n>/ without first blocking in LockPR, whose lock file Layout.PRLockFile nests at locks/<owner>/<repo>/pr-<n>.lock, where it can never collide with the differently named probe lock of §5.6. A released lock keeps its file, because flock binds to an inode and unlinking it would let the next waiter lock a fresh one while the holder still ran, which TestReleasingTheLockKeepsItsFile pins.
- Reads are lock-free per §2.3.2: Layout.ReadPR calls os.ReadFile and takes nothing at all, which is exactly why every write publishes by rename. writeAtomic writes a temporary file beside the target and renames it into place, so a reader holding no lock sees either the previous document or the whole new one, proved by TestALockFreeReadNeverSeesAPartialWrite over 200 rewrites of a 64 KiB document read concurrently by four goroutines.
- TestConcurrentWritersSerialise drives eight goroutines through 25 locked read-modify-writes each and asserts the counter reaches 200, so a single lost update fails it, and TestAReaderProceedsWhileAWriterHoldsTheLock reads the file while a writer holds the lock and fails if that read has not returned within ten seconds. The gate now runs go test -race, changed in one commit across all three places that must agree: spec/0.1.0.tasks.json, TestQualityGateRunsEveryStep and CLAUDE.md.

Out of scope: the per-PR state files of the §2.3 table and the head and round fields of §2.3.3 belong to a later task, as does the probe lock of §5.6.

tasks.title: Create the per-PR state files
tasks.acceptance:
- The per-PR directory holds every file of the §2.3 table: meta.json, claims.ndjson, units.ndjson, mapping.ndjson, posted-index.ndjson, intent-gaps.ndjson, runs.ndjson, threads.ndjson, findings.ndjson, probes.ndjson, coverage.ndjson, transitions.ndjson, and waivers.ndjson.
- meta.json carries PR identity, issue key, profile id, active roles, round index, recorded head, and post_unresolved.
- Each file has a typed reader and writer; no command parses NDJSON inline.
tasks.closed_reason:
- Layout.EnsurePR now creates every file of the §2.3 table — meta.json, claims.ndjson, units.ndjson, mapping.ndjson, posted-index.ndjson, intent-gaps.ndjson, runs.ndjson, threads.ndjson, findings.ndjson, probes.ndjson, coverage.ndjson, transitions.ndjson, waivers.ndjson — named once in internal/state/prfiles.go and asserted in table order by TestEnsurePRCreatesEveryStateFile; creating them is a write to per-PR state, so it happens inside LockPR's exclusive lock (§2.3.1) and publishes through writeAtomic, and TestEnsurePRKeepsRecordedState proves a second ensure never discards a recorded round.
- internal/state/meta.go's Meta carries every part of the §2.3 meta.json row: owner, repo, and pr for the identity, issue_key, profile_id, active_roles, round, head, and post_unresolved, with round 0 documented as a directory no round has been opened in since §9.3.3 starts the count at 1; TestMetaSurvivesARoundTrip asserts all of them survive the writer and the reader, and TestMetaNeverWritesANullRoleList pins active_roles to [] rather than null (§12.3).
- Every file has a typed reader and writer: Layout.ReadMeta and Lock.WriteMeta for meta.json, and the generic ReadRecords, WriteRecords, and WriteStamped for the twelve NDJSON files, which each later schema task instantiates with its own record type. NDJSON is one JSON document per line, an empty file decodes to an empty slice rather than nil, and a line that does not decode is reported by its path and line number.
- No command parses NDJSON inline, because there is no route to a per-PR file that does not pass through these functions: writes are methods and package functions taking the held *Lock, and reads go through Layout.ReadRecords. The head and round stamping of §2.3.3 is a property of the writer rather than of its callers — WriteStamped sets the pair on every record and overwrites whatever it arrived with, WriteRecords refuses one of the eight §2.3.3 files, and WriteStamped refuses a file outside that list, so the four agent-input commands cannot disagree about who owns the fields; a record type opts in by embedding state.Stamp, whose unexported setStamp makes the Stamped interface unimplementable from outside the package. The later stamp-head-round-fields task adds its rejection of an agent-supplied head or round in that one writer. Gate green: go test -race ./... && golangci-lint run && ./scripts/deadcode.sh. Mutation testing: gremlins unleash --timeout-coefficient 30 ./internal gives Killed 125, Lived 2, efficacy 98.43%, above the 98.25% baseline and with no new survivor — the two survivors are the documented internal/config words pair.

tasks.title: Create per-round artefact directories
tasks.acceptance:
- rounds/<n>/ holds draft.md, rendered.json, posted.json, and summary.json, per the §2.3 table.
- The directory is created on demand for the current round index and earlier rounds are never touched.
- A test asserts round 2 artefacts do not disturb round 1.
tasks.closed_reason:
- internal/state/rounds.go names the rounds/<n>/ part of the §2.3 table in table order, draft.md then rendered.json then posted.json then summary.json, and EnsureRound publishes all four inside one round directory, the three JSON artefacts carrying an empty document rather than the unparseable empty file an NDJSON artefact starts from, with typed access through RoundDir, RoundFile, ReadRound, WriteRound and UpdateRoundJSON, whose read-modify-write shape lets each of §10.3's three writers set its own counts without rewriting the whole document. TestARoundDirectoryHoldsEveryArtefact asserts the set, the order and the initial contents, TestLayoutDerivesEveryRoundPath the paths, TestEachWriterUpdatesOnlyItsOwnSummarySection the accumulation, and TestOnlyTheTablesArtefactsReachARoundDirectory refuses any name the table does not give a round.
- A round directory appears only when that round is first written. EnsurePR opens none, and EnsureRound creates exactly the round index it is handed, under the §2.3.1 lock and through the atomic publish of §2.3.2, leaving an artefact that is already there as it is. No path it composes names another round and the package offers no way to clear or enumerate rounds, so §9.3.5's requirement that a command replacing or clearing a file leaves earlier rounds intact holds by construction. Round 0 is refused on every route in, because §9.3.3 opens the count at 1 and meta.json's 0 means no round has been opened, which TestRoundZeroIsNotARound pins together with the absence of rounds/0 on disk.
- TestASecondRoundLeavesTheFirstIntact fills all four of round 1's artefacts, snapshots them, writes all four of round 2's, and asserts round 1's files come back byte-identical while round 2 holds its own.

tasks.title: Stamp head fields on state records
tasks.acceptance:
- Every record in claims.ndjson, units.ndjson, mapping.ndjson, findings.ndjson, probes.ndjson, runs.ndjson, intent-gaps.ndjson, and coverage.ndjson carries head and round, per §2.3.3.
- Round 8 finding head-round-stamping-unassigned: head and round are stamped by cr on write for every file §2.3.3 lists, and MUST NOT be supplied by the agent. A record arriving with either is rejected with exit code 1 naming the line and the field, exactly as §6.1.4 rejects grade.
- The stamping happens in one shared writer so the four agent-input commands (claims record, map record, cells record, record) cannot disagree about who owns the fields.
- A test supplies head and round through each of the four commands and asserts all four reject.
tasks.closed_reason:
- Every record of claims.ndjson, units.ndjson, mapping.ndjson, findings.ndjson, probes.ndjson, runs.ndjson, intent-gaps.ndjson and coverage.ndjson carries head and round per §2.3.3: a record type opts in by embedding state.Stamp, and state.WriteStamped, the only writer those eight files accept, sets the pair on every record on the way out. TestAFileIsWrittenThroughTheWriterItsSchemaRequires pins the routing in both directions and TestDecodedRecordsAreStampedOnTheWayOut reads the stamped pair back off disk.
- Round 8 finding head-round-stamping-unassigned is assigned. Spec §2.3.3 now states that cr writes head and round on every write to the eight files it lists and rejects a record that arrives carrying either, so the authorship the finding found unassigned is written down in the normative document as well as in the code, and state.WriteStamped overwrites whatever a record arrived holding.
- A record supplying either field is refused at decode time on the wire, because §2.3.3 fields arrive inside agent-authored NDJSON and a struct that already decoded cannot report which keys were present. state.DecodeStamped refuses any line whose JSON object holds the key head or round, returning a state.ReservedFieldError that names the file, the one-based line counted over the file as handed in, and the field, and internal/cli/exit.go maps it onto ExitValidation, which is exit code 1 exactly as §6.1.4 rejects grade. The check is presence rather than a non-zero Go field, because an empty head and a zero round are values the agent chose. TestAnAgentMayNotSupplyHeadOrRound covers both degenerate values, a null head, real values, and a record supplying both, and TestASuppliedStampFieldExitsWithTheValidationCode asserts the code survives the wrapping a command adds on the way out.
- The stamping and the rejection live in one shared writer, so the four agent-input commands cannot disagree about who owns the fields: state.WriteStamped is the only function that sets the pair, state.DecodeStamped is the only road from an agent file into it, WriteRecords refuses the eight §2.3.3 files and WriteStamped refuses every other file. cr claims record, cr map record, cr cells record and cr record inherit both behaviours the day each lands instead of restating them.
- Reported rather than faked: none of the four commands exists yet, so no test can supply head and round through them today, and a test against a stub would assert nothing. The rejection is instead implemented and tested at the single point all four must pass through, by three state tests and one cli test covering the presence check, the line number, the field name and the exit code. Gate: go test -race ./... ok, golangci-lint 0 issues, scripts/deadcode.sh clean. Mutation testing with gremlins unleash --timeout-coefficient 30 ./internal moved from the recorded baseline of Killed 125, Lived 2, 98.43 per cent to Killed 131, Lived 2, 98.50 per cent, with no new survivor. The two survivors remain the documented internal/config words pair, and the single TIMED OUT mutant at state/layout.go:233, where negating the LockPR error check returns early while still holding the flock, was confirmed pre-existing by running gremlins on HEAD~7 in a scratch worktree.
Out of scope: the end-to-end assertion the fourth criterion asks for belongs to the tasks that build the commands, and each must assert that a supplied head or round exits 1 naming the line and the field: claims-record-command, map-record-command, cells-record-command, and finding-required-field-validation, which owns the validation for cr record.

tasks.title: Resolve configuration through five layers
tasks.acceptance:
- Effective configuration resolves at read time in the §2.7 order, highest first: command-line flags, CR_-prefixed environment variables, per-repository config, global config, built-in defaults.
- cr config prints the effective configuration.
- A test sets the same key at each of the five layers and asserts the winner at every depth.
tasks.closed_reason:
- Effective configuration now resolves at read time in internal/config/config.go, where Resolve seeds the built-in defaults and then applies the global config, the per-repository config, the CR_-prefixed environment, and the command-line flags in that order, so the highest layer of §2.7 wins, and any CR_ variable or config key whose name addresses the confirmation gate, the argued forcing, or the question label is rejected naming the decision it would reach, while CR_HOME passes through as the state root rather than a setting.
- cr config prints the effective configuration as pretty JSON keyed by the dotted §2.7 names, wired in internal/cli/config.go and internal/cli/root.go, reading the global config from the state layout and the per-repository config when --repo owner/repo is given, exercised with the freshly built binary against a scratch CR_HOME where the repository layer beat the global layer, 7 over 9, and a protected CR_POST_AUTO_CONFIRM was refused with exit code 2.
- TestResolutionPrefersTheHighestLayer sets post.max_comments at all five layers and strips the winning layer at each step, asserting 30 for flags, 25 for the environment, 15 for the per-repository config, 10 for the global config, and 20 for the built-in default, with TestProtectedNamesAreRejected, TestLayerValuesAreCoercedToTheSettingType, and TestConfigCommandPrintsTheEffectiveConfiguration covering the refusal, the per-layer typing, and the command output.
Out of scope: cr config --resolved and its per-setting layer annotation belong to config-resolved-annotation, so the resolver records no layer origin yet.

tasks.title: Annotate settings with their source layer
tasks.acceptance:
- cr config --resolved annotates every setting with the layer that supplied it, per §2.7.
- The annotation names the actual file path or environment variable, not just the layer's rank.
- A test asserts the annotation changes when the same key is moved between layers.

tasks.title: Reject configuration keys addressing protected rules
tasks.acceptance:
- The confirmation gate of §8.5, the argued forcing of §6.3, and the question label of §8.1.4 are not settings and MUST NOT be readable from any layer.
- cr rejects and reports any CR_-prefixed variable or config key whose name would address any of them.
- The rejection is a deny-list check on key names at read time; a test asserts each of the three is unreachable from an environment variable and from both config files.
- Round 11 finding unprotected-disclosure-channel, assigned here: §2.7's protected list names the gate, the forcing, and the §8.1.4 label but not the §8.1.6 provenance or §8.1.7 evidence regions, though both are the sole channels carrying disclosure and checkability to the author. The implementation protects all five from every configuration layer.
tasks.closed_reason:
- The confirmation gate of §8.5, the argued forcing of §6.3 and the question label of §8.1.4 stay unreadable from every layer of §2.7: internal/config/config.go keeps the whole configuration surface in the settings table, no entry of which names any of them, and TestNoFlagLayerCanIntroduceAProtectedSetting fails the moment a built-in key does, so no config file, environment variable or flag can reach one.
- cr rejects and reports any CR_-prefixed variable or config key addressing one: checkProtected raises ProtectedError naming the variable or key as written and the decision it would have reached, the file layers prefix the path, and internal/cli/exit.go maps ProtectedError onto ExitFile because §11.2 codes a configuration failure 3 rather than a usage error the invocation could fix, proven by TestProtectedConfigNameExitsWithTheFileCode and by the built binary exiting 3 on CR_POST_AUTO_CONFIRM and on a config.json carrying render.evidence_region.
- The rejection is a deny-list check on names at read time inside Resolve, before any value is used: §2.7 refuses a name that would address a decision, which I read as neither an exact key list, defeated by any synonym, nor any occurrence of the letters, which would refuse rules.aggregate_min and blame the confirmation gate for it, so a name is split into its words and a word carrying a token is refused, leaving post.gate_timeout_seconds and post.labels refused, since over-refusing costs a rename while under-refusing costs an implicit network write.
- A test asserts each protected decision is unreachable from an environment variable and from both config files: TestProtectedNamesAreRejected drives seven names through the environment, the global config and the per-repository config and checks the reported name and subject, TestOnlyTheStateRootIsExemptFromTheProtectedScan proves CR_HOME is exempt by equality against one constant and that the exemption grants no immunity because CR_HOME passes the scan on its own spelling, TestNoFlagLayerCanIntroduceAProtectedSetting proves the flag exemption §8.5.2 requires cannot leak into the environment or file layers, and every guard was watched failing with the gate token removed, the forcing token removed, the exemption widened to a prefix and a protected built-in key added.
- Round 11 finding unprotected-disclosure-channel named the gap: §2.7 protects the gate, the forcing and the §8.1.4 label but not the §8.1.6 provenance region or the §8.1.7 evidence region, the two channels through which disclosure and checkability reach the author, so a config key silencing either would have removed the honesty the assertion register rests on.
- The implementation protects all five from every configuration layer: the token table now carries provenance and evidence beside confirm, gate, argued, forcing and label, the package comment records why, TestProtectedNamesAreRejected covers all five across the environment and both config files, and flatten now keeps the key an empty object leaves behind so a name cannot slip past the scan by carrying no value.

tasks.title: Guard that no model client exists
tasks.acceptance:
- Invariant 1: cr never calls a language model. No API client, no model name, no inference.
- A guard test greps the module's dependency graph and source for model provider clients and model identifiers, failing when one appears.
- go.mod carries no model SDK dependency.
tasks.closed_reason:
- Invariant 1 is enforced in Go rather than documented. internal/cli/nomodel_test.go fences the three ways a language model can reach cr — an SDK sitting in the module graph, an SDK inside the compiled closure, and a model endpoint or identifier written by hand — so §2.1.1's reproducibility now has a mechanical reason to hold rather than a stated one, and the register cr asserts in stays backed by what it established itself.
- No API client, no model name, and no inference survives any of the three checks. A constructed client is caught as an import, a hand-rolled call is caught by its host and request path, and a model name is caught by its family prefix, with credential names listed alongside the hosts because they are the same call one step earlier. The scope is what executes, not what is written: prose is deliberately outside, because CLAUDE.md, §1.3.4, §2.1, and thirteen rounds under spec/.tp-review/ are the documents that state the invariant and a repository-wide grep would convict exactly them. §3.1's tracker command and a user's own profile are outside for the opposite reason, being argv the user supplies at runtime, while §2.4.5's built-in profiles are inside, because they ship in the binary and name commands cr runs itself.
- A guard test reads both the dependency graph and the source, failing when a provider client or a model identifier appears. TestNoModelSDKSitsInTheModuleGraph scans go.mod and go.sum as text, which needs no network and catches a transitive module nobody chose. TestNothingCrBuildsImportsAModelSDK scans go list -deps -test ./..., which sees through a dependency in a way cr's own import blocks cannot. TestNoModelEndpointOrIdentifierReachesTheBinary walks every .go file plus the assets they //go:embed, with the guard file excluded from its own surface and a floor on the files scanned so a misresolved root cannot pass vacuously. Each was watched to fail on a real violating input and then reverted: a fake anthropic module appended to go.sum, then that module required and replaced with a local package and blank-imported from internal/cli, then a hand-written api.anthropic.com constant in a .go file together with a gpt-4o string added to the embedded generic profile. The graph guard alone fired for the required-but-unimported case, which keeps the weaker fault distinguishable from the stronger one while still failing it, since the distance between the two is one import line.

Its require blocks hold cobra, flock, testify and their indirects and nothing else, and that is now asserted rather than observed, proven by appending a fake anthropic-sdk-go line to go.sum and watching the graph guard name the file, the line number, and the matched fragment.
Out of scope: §2.1.2's network-write boundary and §2.1.3's six agent-only judgements are network-write-boundary-guard and agent-only-judgement-guard. The guard does not scan scripts/ or .github/workflows/, which execute in CI rather than inside cr. gremlins unleash --timeout-coefficient 30 ./internal is unchanged at Killed 260, Lived 4, efficacy 98.48% with the one known state/layout.go timeout, as expected from a unit that adds no production branch.

tasks.title: Validate count pattern group arity

tasks.title: Define the probe path template
tasks.acceptance:

- The template's placeholder vocabulary is enumerated and closed: <probe-id> and <ext>, nothing else. <probe-id> MUST appear exactly once, as §5.1.6 requires.
- Each shipped profile sets the template explicitly so the result matches its own tests.globs; a test asserts the resolved path for each shipped profile satisfies its own globs.
- A test asserts the §5.1.6 leftover glob — the template with every placeholder substituted except <probe-id>, which becomes * — matches a real artefact path on disk.
tasks.closed_reason:

The default roots at the first glob's literal prefix, placing the file directly under tests/, which Laravel's phpunit.xml registers under no testsuite, and the Test.php suffix is what makes Pest collect the file at all. tasks.acceptance:

- A test asserts a rule-produced record round-trips its rule id through merge and record.

tasks.title: Make rule rationale quotable to authors
tasks.acceptance:

- globs narrow the paths a rule applies to and exempt excludes paths for legacy areas.
- A test asserts a pattern matching a removed line and a pattern matching an unchanged repository line both produce no hit.

tasks.title: Compile detect patterns as Go regexp

tasks.title: Record a hit as citation
tasks.acceptance:
- A hit is recorded as a citations entry per §6.1 carrying the matched path, line, and origin: rule, which grades the record cited per §6.2, per §2.6.1.3.

- A test asserts a hit produces a citation whose origin cr stamped, never one the agent supplied.

tasks.title: Inject detect-less rules into prompts
tasks.acceptance:

- A test asserts a detect-less rule's title and rationale appear in the emitted prompt.

tasks.title: Drop hits the agent never confirms
tasks.acceptance:
- Detection reports hits, never verdicts. A hit reaches a draft only when the agent explicitly confirms it; an unconfirmed hit is dropped, not posted, per §2.6.1.5.
- Confirmation is what a rule cannot supply for itself, so no detect block buys the assertion register of §6.3 on its own.
- A test runs detection producing three hits, has the agent confirm one, and asserts two never reach findings.ndjson.

tasks.title: Append rule events idempotently to ledger
tasks.acceptance:
- Every hit, record, and dismissal is appended to rule-stats.ndjson with the rule id, the matched path and line, the round, and the head, per §2.6.1.6. The path and line are load-bearing: §6.2.5 matches a citation against this file positionally, and a rule id alone would let any citation claim any hit.

- Round 9 finding rule-stats-event-producer: cr record is named as the producer of a dismissal event, writing one per current-round hit that no recorded record cites — the observable moment §2.6.1.5's drop otherwise lacks.
- A test runs detection twice in one round and asserts the ledger holds one entry per hit, not two.

tasks.title: Generate a suggestion from fix
tasks.acceptance:
- A rule may carry fix.replace and fix.with as a regular expression and its replacement, applied to the matched line to produce a suggestion, per §2.6.2.1.
- A generated suggestion passes the validation of §8.2 before drafting; one that fails validation is dropped while its record survives, per §2.6.2.2.
- A test asserts a record outlives its dropped suggestion.

tasks.title: Never apply a fix to files
tasks.acceptance:
- cr never applies a fix to any file. A fix only ever produces suggestion text for the author to accept, per §2.6.2.3.
- A test asserts the working tree is unchanged after a fix-carrying rule hits.

tasks.title: Stamp machine-generated suggestion origin
tasks.acceptance:
- cr cannot establish that a generated replacement compiles, parses, or preserves behaviour. A suggestion produced by fix carries suggestion_origin: rule, is labelled as machine generated in the draft, and is dropped when the agent does not confirm it, per §2.6.2.4.

- A test asserts an unconfirmed machine suggestion never reaches the payload.

tasks.title: Harvest rule candidates from comment history
tasks.acceptance:
- cr rules suggest --repo <owner/repo> scans the bodies of comments posted from recorded rounds and groups them by class and by normalised body per §1.4, per §2.6.3.1.
- A group reaching rules.harvest_min occurrences, default 3, is reported as a candidate rule together with the comments that formed it, per §2.6.3.2.
- A test seeds three matching comments across two rounds and asserts one candidate.

tasks.title: Report rule candidates without writing files
tasks.acceptance:
- Candidates are reported only. cr never writes a rule file by itself, per §2.6.3.3.
- A test asserts ~/.cr/rules/ is unchanged after cr rules suggest.

tasks.title: Report rules dead across recent rounds
tasks.acceptance:
- cr rules list --dead --repo <owner/repo> reports rules that produced no hit and no record across the last rules.dead_after rounds, default 20, so the corpus can be pruned rather than growing without limit, per §2.6.3.4.
- Round 8 finding cross-pr-round-ordering-undefined: the window is defined as the last rules.dead_after distinct (pr, round) pairs ordered by the rule-stats timestamp descending, because round indices are per-PR and PR 7 round 3 is not PR 12 round 3. A rule counts as alive when it produced a hit or a record in any of them.
- cr rules list without --dead reports the effective rules with the layer each came from, per §11.
- A test seeds hits across two pull requests with interleaved timestamps and asserts the window spans both.

tasks.title: Read intent through a configured command
tasks.acceptance:
- intent.cmd is an argv array with a {key} placeholder, defaulting to ["jira", "issue", "view", "{key}", "--plain"], per §3.1.1 and §3.1.2.
- A non-zero exit fails with exit code 3 and surfaces the command's stderr, per §3.1.3.
- cr carries no tracker authentication code; the tracker is read only through this command.

tasks.title: Bypass the tracker with intent file
tasks.acceptance:
- --intent-file <path> bypasses the command and reads the issue text from a file, so the loop works with no tracker access at all, per §3.1.4.
- A test drives a full brief with --intent-file and no tracker command configured.

tasks.title: Resolve the issue key from sources
tasks.acceptance:
- The issue key resolves from the first source that yields a match, in order: the --issue <KEY> flag, the PR branch name, the PR title, the PR body, per §3.2.
- The pattern defaults to [A-Z][A-Z0-9]+-[0-9]+ and is overridable by intent.key_pattern.
- A test asserts each of the four sources wins in turn when the earlier ones carry no match.

tasks.title: Continue without an issue key
tasks.acceptance:
- If no key is found, cr continues with an empty intent and marks the intent axis unavailable per §4.5, per §3.2.
- The unavailability is reported through the §4.5.4 honesty channel and survives --quiet.
- A test asserts a keyless PR still briefs successfully.

tasks.title: Define the claim record schema
tasks.acceptance:
- The claim struct carries every row of the §3.3 field table: id of the form <ISSUE-KEY>#c<n>, text, source (description, acceptance, comment, or note), span, note_id, span_hash, issue_hash, head.
- span_hash and issue_hash are computed by cr, never supplied by the agent.
- note_id is required when source is note.

tasks.title: Store claims replacing the round file
tasks.acceptance:
- cr claims record <pr> <file.ndjson> validates and stores claims, replacing claims.ndjson for the current round and clearing mapping.ndjson, per §3.3.1.
- cr computes span_hash and issue_hash itself.
- Clearing the mapping is scoped to the current round; earlier rounds stay intact per §9.3.5.

tasks.title: Validate claim spans against their source
tasks.acceptance:
- For a claim whose source is not note, cr rejects with exit code 1 any claim whose span does not occur in the issue text, per §3.3.1.
- A claim sourced from the context store carries source: note and a note_id, sets span to that note's body, and is validated against the named note rather than the issue text, per §3.3.2. Each claim is checked against exactly one source, so the two rules never collide.
- Such a claim is included in coverage exactly like a tracker claim, but rests on weaker provenance which §8.1.6 requires to reach the reader.
- A test covers a valid tracker span, an invalid tracker span, a valid note span, and a note span checked against the wrong source.

tasks.title: Detect issue text drift per round
tasks.acceptance:
- Drift is detected by re-reading the issue text at the start of every round and comparing its normalised hash to the stored issue_hash, per §3.3.3.
- When they differ, cr reports for each claim whether its span still occurs in the new issue text.
- cr never re-extracts; re-extraction happens only through a new cr claims record.
- A test mutates the issue text between rounds and asserts the per-claim report without any claim changing.

tasks.title: Take the diff against merge base
tasks.acceptance:
- The diff is taken against the PR merge base at the current head, per §3.4.1.
- A test asserts the diff excludes commits that reached the base branch after the PR branched.
tasks.closed_reason:
- internal/git/diff.go takes the diff against the PR merge base at the current head per §3.4.1: DiffAgainstMergeBase resolves the merge base with git merge-base and then diffs that commit against the head, which is exactly what the three-dot base...head form means, and it returns the merge base alongside the patch so §3.7.1 can report the commit the diff was actually taken against. Every invocation is a read, never a write inside the repository under review (invariant 2, §2.2), and it is pinned so §2.1.1 holds on any machine: an allowlisted environment (dropping GIT_DIR, GIT_EXTERNAL_DIFF and their neighbours, keeping PATH and HOME), C locale, GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0, -c overrides for the knobs with no flag, and explicit --no-ext-diff, --no-textconv, --no-color, --no-relative, --diff-algorithm, --unified, --inter-hunk-context, --find-renames, prefixes and submodule flags. A refusing git becomes a git.CommandError carrying the command and its stderr, which internal/cli/exit.go maps onto exit code 3 in the §3.1.3 shape rather than a second mapping of its own.
- TestTheDiffExcludesWorkThatLandedOnTheBaseAfterBranching builds a real fixture repository in which main gained a commit after feature branched, then asserts the patch carries the author's added line, equals the parting commit as its merge base, and names neither the file that landed on main later nor its content. Replacing the resolved merge base with the base branch tip, the two-dot mistake, makes the test fail with somebody-else.txt appearing as a deletion the author never wrote, which was run and observed before the test was committed. Three further tests hold the pinning honest against a configured diff.external, against an ambient GIT_DIR and GIT_EXTERNAL_DIFF, and over the stderr a refusing read surfaces.

tasks.title: Define changed lines per hunk side
tasks.acceptance:
- A changed line is an added or modified RIGHT-side line, and for a hunk that adds none, its removed LEFT-side lines, per §3.4.1.
- Line numbers are RIGHT-side for the first case and LEFT-side for the second.
- A test covers an add-only hunk, a modify hunk, and a delete-only hunk.
tasks.closed_reason:
- ParseHunks in internal/git/hunk.go reads §3.4.1 changed lines out of the patch DiffAgainstMergeBase produces. A hunk's added lines are exactly its added and modified RIGHT-side lines, because a unified diff has no marker of its own for a modification and writes one as a removal and an addition standing together, and a hunk that adds none contributes its removed LEFT-side lines instead. Hunk.Side records which of the two a hunk turned out to be, so §3.4.4 can partition a file's hunks on it without recounting, and the parser refuses a patch outside the shape the pinned diffArgs produce rather than reading it as something else.
- Every ChangedLine carries the side its number is counted on instead of leaving it implicit in which field held it. An added or modified line is numbered at the head from the header's plus-side start, a removed line of an add-nothing hunk in the merge base from the minus-side start, which is why a delete-only hunk is described in merge-base coordinates while every other hunk is described at the head. The header shapes that hide an off-by-one are handled at the source: a count omitted means one line, and a zero count is a position between two lines rather than a line.
- TestChangedLinesCarryTheSideTheyAreNumberedOn drives the real git of the pinned flags over a fixture carrying one hunk of each shape and asserts an add-only hunk gives RIGHT line 4, a modify hunk gives only its head-side line at RIGHT line 2 and never the pre-image it replaced, and a delete-only hunk gives LEFT line 5. TestTheAwkwardShapesOfAHunk adds eleven header and content shapes including a first-line change, a new file, an insertion point, a deleted file, a missing final newline and a patch whose own content looks like file headers. TestAHunkAnswersForItsHeadSideRange pins the §6.2.1 question and TestAPatchThatIsNotOneIsRejected pins five refusals. hunk.go holds 100 percent statement coverage and gremlins leaves no surviving mutant in internal/git.
Out of scope: clustering, ignore.globs exclusion counting, symbol detectability, the oversized split, unit records with the unit hash, and binary listing are each their own later task. A hunk carries the path from its file header, because a hunk that does not know its file cannot be clustered by one later, but rename and exclusion bookkeeping stays with diff-file-exclusions.

tasks.title: Exclude ignored files with binary listing
tasks.acceptance:
- Files matching ignore.globs are excluded and counted as excluded, per §3.4.2.
- Binary and generated files are listed but not clustered, per §3.4.7.
- A test asserts both counts reach cr status without either file producing a unit.

tasks.title: Fall through to adjacency without error
tasks.acceptance:
- An enclosing symbol is detectable only when the profile declares symbols.lang and cr can build a symbol index for the file, per §3.4.3.
- When it cannot, clustering falls through to adjacency without reporting an error.
- A test runs clustering under the generic profile, which declares no symbols.lang, and asserts adjacency clustering with no error.

tasks.title: Cluster hunks by symbol then adjacency
tasks.acceptance:
- Clustering first partitions a file's hunks by the side their changed lines sit on per §3.4.1; adjacency, the §3.4.5 split, and the §3.4.6 hash order compare line numbers only within one side, and a unit never mixes sides, per §3.4.4.
- Hunks are then clustered by, in order: same file and same enclosing symbol when detectable; otherwise same file and adjacency, where two hunks are adjacent when the gap between the last changed line of one and the first changed line of the next is at most cluster.gap_lines (default 12); otherwise one unit per hunk.
- A test covers all three branches and asserts no unit ever mixes sides.

tasks.title: Split clusters exceeding the line cap
tasks.acceptance:
- A cluster exceeding cluster.max_lines changed lines (default 80) is split by taking its hunks in ascending start order and opening a new unit whenever adding the next hunk would exceed the limit, per §3.4.5.
- A single hunk that alone exceeds the limit becomes one unit, is flagged oversized, and appears as such in the coverage report; it is the one case where the limit does not bind.
- A test covers a splittable cluster and an unsplittable oversized hunk.

tasks.title: Record unit fields with the hash
tasks.acceptance:
- Every unit records an id of the form u<n>, its file paths, its hunk ranges, its changed line count, a unit hash, and whether it was formed by symbol, by adjacency, or by fallback, per §3.4.6.
- The unit hash is the normalised hash per §1.4 of the unit's changed lines taken file by file in ascending path order and, within a file, ascending line order, joined by LF.
- A test fixes the hash for a known unit and asserts it changes when a changed line changes.

tasks.title: Order unit ids with side tiebreak
tasks.acceptance:
- Unit ids are round-scoped, assigned in ascending order of first file path then first changed line, and are not carried across rounds, per §3.4.6.
- Round 8 finding non-total-ordering: the id ordering is the one comparison that ranges over both sides at once, so it carries a side tiebreak — first file path ascending, then side with LEFT before RIGHT matching §8.3.3's convention, then first changed line ascending. Without it a file holding both a RIGHT-sided and a LEFT-sided unit yields two units whose first changed line is the same number in two coordinate spaces, the ordering is not total, and §2.1.1's reproducibility fails.
- Round 8 finding vacuous-multi-file-unit: since every branch of §3.4.4 clusters within one file, a unit carries exactly one file path. The implementation pins this — §3.4.6's per-file hash ordering and §6.2.1's path-membership test are written against a single-path unit and a test asserts no constructible diff yields two.
- A test builds a file with a delete-only hunk and an add-only hunk at the same line number and asserts a stable, total id assignment across repeated runs.

tasks.title: Ingest every existing review thread
tasks.acceptance:
- All existing review threads on the PR are ingested, including resolved ones, with author, body, anchor, resolution state, and replies, per §3.5.1.
- Threads are stored in threads.ndjson per §2.3.
- A test ingests a PR carrying resolved and unresolved threads and asserts both survive.
tasks.closed_reason:
- Every existing review thread on the pull request is ingested with author, body, anchor, resolution state and replies (§3.5.1): internal/gh/threads.go asks GitHub's GraphQL API for reviewThreads, the only place isResolved exists at all — REST's pull request review comments carry no resolution, so a resolved thread could only be guessed at — and walks both connections, following further pages of threads by cursor and a long thread's further comments by node id, so nothing is silently truncated; a thread keeps its opening comment as its author and body, the rest as replies, and its anchor normalised into path, side, start_line and line in git.Side terms §3.5.3 can compare against a hunk, with the original pair kept for an outdated thread whose current line GitHub reports null.
- Threads are stored in threads.ndjson per §2.3: gh.WriteThreads names that file once and writes it through internal/state's WriteRecords, the writer for the files §2.3.3 does not stamp with head and round, under the §2.3.1 lock, and TestThreadsAreStoredInThreadsNdjson round-trips the ingest and pins the empty reply list as [] rather than null per §12.3.
- A test ingests a pull request carrying resolved and unresolved threads and asserts both survive: TestIngestionKeepsResolvedAndUnresolvedThreadsAlike replays the recorded payload of cli/cli#11451 — one resolved bot thread, one unresolved human thread with a reply — and asserts both threads, their ids, authors, bodies, anchors, replies and resolution states; every test in internal/gh runs offline, from fixtures under testdata captured once by hand from public pull requests and replayed through the injectable Runner seam, with a shell stub named gh on PATH for the three tests that exercise the real invocation, its allowlisted environment and its failure shape.

tasks.title: Tag threads as human or bot
tasks.acceptance:
- Each thread is tagged with an author type of human or bot, per §3.5.2.
- cr never assigns a class to an ingested thread, per §3.5.3.
tasks.closed_reason:
- Every ingested thread carries §3.5.2's tag: internal/gh/threads.go adds the AuthorType type with AuthorHuman and AuthorBot, a Thread.AuthorType field serialised as author_type, and authorType(), which Client.thread() applies to every thread it builds, including one whose opening comment is missing. The rule is GitHub's own answer and nothing added to it, so only __typename Bot becomes bot while a User, an Organization, a Mannequin, and an author the API answers null for all become human. That leaves dependabot[bot] posting as a User tagged human, deliberately: reading a [bot] suffix or carrying a login allowlist would be cr deciding whose comment counts, which §2.1 leaves to the agent, and it fails in the expensive direction, because a human wrongly tagged bot loses §3.5.3's attachment and the §3.5.4 suppression built on it, so cr repeats a concern a colleague already raised. TestEveryIngestedThreadIsTaggedHumanOrBot pins the Bot and User threads of the recorded fixture and TestOnlyGitHubsOwnBotTypeIsTaggedBot pins all four judgement cases.
- cr assigns no class to an ingested thread, and the negative is mechanically held rather than merely true today: TestNoIngestedThreadCarriesAClass walks gh.Thread reflectively against threadFields, the exact §3.5.1 plus §3.5.2 field surface with no class among them, and also marshals a Thread and asserts the wire carries no class key, so both a struct field added years from now and a hand-written marshaller fail it. The guard was verified by temporarily adding a Class string field, which failed both assertions before it was reverted. gremlins unleash --timeout-coefficient 30 ./internal reports Killed 254, Lived 4, efficacy 98.45 percent, the four survivors being the known commented baseline in internal/config and internal/finding, with the new authorType conditional at gh/threads.go:399 killed.

tasks.title: Attach nearby human threads to units
tasks.acceptance:
- cr attaches to every unit the ingested human threads whose anchor falls inside the unit's hunks or within threads.proximity_lines (default 10) of them, per §3.5.3.
- cr never decides suppression itself; it locates the candidate and supplies it.
- A test asserts a bot thread and a thread beyond the proximity window are both left unattached.

tasks.title: Record a finding suppressed by thread
tasks.acceptance:
- The agent decides whether an attached thread already covers a finding. When it does, the finding is recorded in state suppressed carrying suppressed_by with the thread id, and is not drafted, per §3.5.4.
- The decision arrives through the record input, never from a cr-side text match.
- A test asserts a suppressed record never reaches draft.md.

tasks.title: Offer author replies as candidate notes
tasks.acceptance:
- Author replies inside ingested threads are offered as candidate context notes per §3.6, per §3.5.5.
- They are offered, never written: recording one is cr note with source thread.
- A test asserts a reply appears as a candidate without a note file being created.

tasks.title: Append a note against an issue
tasks.acceptance:
- cr note <ISSUE-KEY> "<text>" --source <source> appends a note with an id of the form <ISSUE-KEY>#n<n>, a timestamp, the PR it came from, and the source, per §3.6.1.
- Valid sources are chat, jira, thread, meeting, and other, per §3.6.3; any other value is rejected.
- The context store holds facts that are true about the issue but absent from the tracker.
- Round 11 finding unspecified-flag-requiredness, assigned here: §3.6.1 shows --source in the synopsis but never says it is required. The implementation requires it and rejects an absent or unlisted value with exit code 2.

tasks.title: Store an answer as a note
tasks.acceptance:
- cr answer <pr> <record-id> "<text>" --source <source> appends a note referencing that record, so the answer to a posted question is captured against the issue key rather than lost in a thread, per §3.6.2.
- It does not change the record's state: v0.1 ends at posting per §9, and whether an answer settles a question is a judgement v0.2 makes.
- A test asserts the referenced record's state is byte-identical before and after.

tasks.title: Print accumulated notes with provenance
tasks.acceptance:
- cr context <ISSUE-KEY> prints the accumulated notes with provenance, per §3.6.5.
- Notes for the issue key are loaded automatically on every subsequent round and every subsequent PR that resolves to the same key, per §3.6.4.
- A test asserts a note recorded against PR 1 loads for PR 2 sharing the issue key.

tasks.title: Retract a note within the round
tasks.acceptance:
- A note is unverified hearsay and stays revocable. cr note --remove <note-id> retracts one, and any coverage cell or record citing a retracted note is reported as needing re-evaluation in the next round rather than silently retained, per §3.6.6.
- Round 9 finding retracted-provenance-still-posts: retraction takes effect in the round it happens, not only in the next one. On cr note --remove, every current-round record or cell citing that note is re-evaluated immediately — the record is forced to kind: question or blocked from drafting, so a reviewer who retracts a note precisely because they learned it was wrong cannot still have cr draft and cr post --confirm send the assertion built on it. Because v0.1 ends at posting, the next round may never arrive for this pull request.
- Round 9 finding retracted-provenance-still-posts: a record resting on a retracted note no longer has provenance to disclose, so it no longer qualifies for the assertion register and §8.1.6's provenance region is not emitted for a dangling note id.
- The retraction is reported by cr status and in the round summary, in addition to the next-round report §3.6.6 already requires. The record itself is retained so the decision stays auditable.
- A test retracts a note mid-round and asserts the dependent record is a question, is reported, and cannot be posted as a finding.

tasks.title: Create per-PR state on first brief
tasks.acceptance:
- Round 8 finding state-file-without-mandated-writer: cr brief creates meta.json with the round index starting at 1 and the recorded head set to the current head, and persists units.ndjson and threads.ndjson for the current round. §3.7's permission to persist derived inputs becomes an obligation, because §4.5.6 and §4.1.6 reject unknown unit ids, §9.3.1 and §9.3.3 read meta.json, and §3.5.3 attaches ingested threads — all treating these files as authoritative.
- Every other command that reads them fails with exit code 4 and a hint naming cr brief when they are absent, rather than recomputing units on the fly.
- A test runs cr review, cr cells record, and cr map record against a PR that was never briefed and asserts all three exit 4 with the hint.

tasks.title: Print the six-part orientation payload
tasks.acceptance:
- cr brief assembles and prints, without judgement, all six items of §3.7: PR identity, head SHA, merge base, and the resolved profile with the layer that selected it; the issue key and the source it resolved from, with the issue text or the reason no key was found; the claims of §3.3 and whether the issue text has drifted; the units of §3.4 with file paths, hunk ranges, and unit hashes; the ingested threads of §3.5 and the notes of §3.6; the active, disabled, and unavailable axes with their reasons per §4.5.
- A test asserts all six sections appear in both the text and JSON renderings.

tasks.title: Keep brief free of judgement artefacts
tasks.acceptance:
- cr brief is read-only with respect to judgement: it performs no network write and creates no finding, coverage cell, probe, or thread, per §3.7.
- It may compute and persist the derived inputs of §3.3 through §3.6 because those are facts about the PR rather than opinions about it, and §4.6 needs the same unit set.
- A test asserts findings.ndjson, coverage.ndjson, and probes.ndjson are untouched by a brief.

tasks.title: Make brief idempotent at unchanged head
tasks.acceptance:
- At an unchanged head cr brief is idempotent, per §3.7 and §9.3.3.
- When the head has moved it opens a new round per §9.3.3, which is the one case where it changes state.
- A test runs brief twice at one head and asserts the state directory is byte-identical.

tasks.title: Store the claim-to-unit mapping
tasks.acceptance:
- The claim-to-unit mapping is the agent's judgement. cr map record <pr> <file.ndjson> replaces mapping.ndjson for the current round with one {claim, unit} pair per line, rejecting an unknown claim or unit id with exit code 1, per §4.1.6.
- Every rule in §4.1 through §4.4 that speaks of the claims a unit is mapped to reads this file.
- Every unit is mapped to zero or more claims, per §4.1.1.
- Replacement is scoped to the current round; earlier rounds stay intact per §9.3.5.

tasks.title: Raise an unmapped unit as question
tasks.acceptance:
- A unit mapped to zero claims raises an unmapped-unit item, per §4.1.2.
- An unmapped unit defaults to a question, never a finding, because the most common cause is intent that never reached the tracker, per §4.1.4.
- A test asserts an unmapped unit's record arrives as kind: question even before §6.3's forcing runs.

tasks.title: Attach issue notes to unmapped units
tasks.acceptance:
- cr attaches the issue key's notes to every unmapped unit, per §4.1.5.
- The agent decides whether a note explains the unit; when it does, the item is not raised and the coverage cell cites the note id.
- cr never decides this by matching text.
- A test asserts a recorded note suppresses the matching unmapped-unit question only when the agent says so, and that the resulting cell carries note_id.

tasks.title: Write unimplemented claims to gaps file
tasks.acceptance:
- A claim mapped to zero units raises an unimplemented-claim entry. It has no code location by construction, so it cannot be a coverage cell — §4.5.5 requires every cell to name a unit — and is instead written to intent-gaps.ndjson carrying claim, round, head, and set_aside_note when §10.2.3 applies, per §4.1.3.
- It is reported by cr status per §10.1.2 and blocks completeness per §10.2.3.
- A test asserts the entry carries all four fields with head and round stamped by cr.

tasks.title: Keep intent gaps out of findings
tasks.acceptance:
- An unimplemented-claim entry never becomes a record in findings.ndjson, and is never drafted or posted: v0.1 has no unanchored comment channel per §1.6.1, per §4.1.3.
- The reviewer raises it with the author out of band and may record the answer as a note per §3.6.
- A test asserts a gap entry reaches cr status and reaches neither draft.md nor the posted payload.

tasks.title: Derive gaps preserving set-aside stamps
tasks.acceptance:
- On each successful cr map record, cr derives intent-gaps.ndjson mechanically as the claims of the current round mapped to zero units, per §4.1.7.
- Round 9 finding derived-state-clobbers-decision: because §4.1.6 permits re-recording the mapping, re-derivation preserves set_aside_note for any claim that is still unmapped, and drops the stamp — reporting that it did — for a claim that has since become mapped. A literal re-derivation would silently discard every set-aside decision the reviewer made and re-block §10.2.3 with no report.
- The surviving-stamp count is reported by cr status per §10.1.2, so the preservation is observable rather than assumed.
- A test sets a claim aside, re-records the mapping unchanged, and asserts the stamp survives; then maps that claim to a unit, re-records, and asserts the stamp is dropped with a report.
- Round 12 finding derived-file-erases-recorded-decision, re-reported: a literal mechanical re-derivation discards every set_aside_note the reviewer recorded and silently re-imposes §10.2.3's completeness block. The carry-forward rule above is what prevents it.

tasks.title: Set an unimplemented claim aside
tasks.acceptance:
- cr claims set-aside <pr> <claim-id> --note <note-id> stamps set_aside_note on that gap entry after checking the note exists for the PR's issue key, per §4.1.8.
- Judging a claim out of scope is the agent's call, never cr's; cr only validates the note reference.
- A test asserts a set-aside naming a nonexistent note is rejected with exit code 1.

tasks.title: Evaluate units against their mapped claims
tasks.acceptance:
- Each unit is evaluated against the claims it is mapped to, per §4.2.1.
- A correctness finding cites the claim id it violates, per §4.2.2.
- A unit mapped to zero claims is still evaluated for internal defects, per §4.2.3.
- A test asserts a zero-claim unit still produces a prompt on the correctness axis.

tasks.title: Build a head symbol index
tasks.acceptance:
- cr builds a symbol index for the head from the profile's symbols.lang, per §4.3.1.
- For every function, method, or class added by the diff, cr attaches candidate pre-existing symbols drawn from the head symbol index minus every symbol the diff itself declares on a changed line.
- A test asserts a symbol the diff declares never appears as its own candidate.

tasks.title: Mark reinvention unavailable without an index
tasks.acceptance:
- When no symbol index can be built, the reinvention half of the convention axis is marked unavailable per §4.5 rather than skipped silently, per §4.3.1.
- The unavailability appears in the coverage report with its reason and survives --quiet per §11.1.
- A test runs the convention axis under the generic profile and asserts the reinvention half is reported unavailable while the rest of the axis still runs.

tasks.title: Rank candidates by comparison name similarity
tasks.acceptance:
- Candidate ranking works on the comparison name: the symbol name case-folded to lowercase with every _ and - removed, per §4.3.2.
- Similarity is 1 - levenshtein(a, b) / max(len(a), len(b)) over comparison names, counted in Unicode code points, defined as 1.0 when both names are empty.
- A candidate qualifies only when its similarity is at least reinvention.min_similarity (default 0.6) and its declared parameter count equals that of the added symbol. The declared parameter count of a function or method is the number of parameters in its signature; for a class it is the parameter count of its constructor, or zero when it declares none.
- Qualifying candidates are ordered by similarity descending, then path ascending, then line ascending, and cr attaches at most reinvention.max_candidates (default 5).
- Semantic equivalence is the agent's judgement, not cr's; a test asserts cr emits candidates and no verdict.

tasks.title: Default reinvention items to question kind
tasks.acceptance:
- A reinvention item cites the candidate symbol as path:line, per §4.3.3.
- Reinvention items default to kind: question, because the tool cannot know whether the existing symbol was rejected for a reason, per §4.3.4.
- A test asserts the default holds before §6.3's forcing is applied.

tasks.title: Attach mechanical rule hits to units
tasks.acceptance:
- Project conventions beyond reinvention come from the rule corpus of §2.6, never from hard-coded logic and never from prose buried inside role instructions, per §4.3.5.
- A mechanical rule hit is attached to the unit that contains it, so the agent judges an already-located candidate instead of searching for one, per §4.3.6.
- A test asserts a hit outside every unit's hunks is not attached to an unrelated unit.

tasks.title: Attach changed test files per unit
tasks.acceptance:
- cr attaches to every unit the test files changed or added by the PR and the symbols they reference, per §4.4.1.
- The agent classifies the unit as covered, partially covered, or uncovered, and the classification is recorded in the coverage cell together with the test paths it rested on.
- cr performs no coverage classification of its own, per §2.1.3.
- Round 12 finding missing-unavailability-path, assigned here: §4.4.1's 'the symbols they reference' needs a symbol index the shipped generic profile cannot provide, and §4.4 states no unavailability path the way §4.3.1 does. The implementation marks that half unavailable with its reason through §4.5.4 rather than failing or silently skipping.

tasks.title: Move edge-case guidance into role instructions
tasks.acceptance:
- Round 8 finding unconsumed-agent-output and round 10 finding orphaned-clause, resolved by approved decision: §4.4's edge-case enumeration obligation and test.max_edge_cases were removed from the specification, and so was the orphaned 'A missing edge case SHOULD be escalated to a probe' clause left behind. §4.4 now holds two items. The shipped test-adequacy role's instructions carry edge-case reasoning as role-owned guidance, and no configuration key named test.max_edge_cases resolves.
- The shipped test-adequacy role's instructions carry edge-case reasoning as role-owned guidance, where a heuristic belongs.
- A test asserts no configuration key named test.max_edge_cases resolves and that the role's instructions mention edge cases.

tasks.title: Deny cited grade to test citations
tasks.acceptance:
- §4.4.2: a test-adequacy finding asserts only with an experiment; citations to test files never grade it cited, so without a supporting probe it is argued and posted as a question per §6.3.
- A test-adequacy finding asserts only with an experiment. Citations to test files never grade it cited, so without a supporting probe it is argued and is posted as a question per §6.3, per §4.4.3.
- A test asserts a test-adequacy record carrying only test-file citations grades argued.
- §6.2's cited row carries ', and the record's axis is not test', so cited is unreachable for the whole test axis and a test-adequacy record is exactly probed or argued. A test asserts both outcomes.

tasks.title: Activate axes from configuration with prerequisites
tasks.acceptance:
- An axis is active when it is enabled by the resolved configuration and its prerequisites are met, per §4.5.1.
- The test axis is disabled automatically when the profile declares no tests.cmd, per §4.5.2.
- The intent axis is marked unavailable when no issue key resolves, per §4.5.3.
- A test covers an enabled axis, a config-disabled axis, an auto-disabled test axis, and an unavailable intent axis.

tasks.title: Define role activeness without circularity
tasks.acceptance:
- Round 8 finding circular-definition: a role is active when its axis is active and its profiles list is empty or names the resolved profile. §4.6.4's skip report is the reporting obligation for the negative case, not an input to the definition — otherwise activeness is defined in terms of an output of the command that consumes it, and §4.5.6 and §10.2.2 need the active set independently of whether cr review has run.
- The command that computes and stores meta.json's active-role list is named, and it is the only writer of that field.
- A test computes the active set with cr review never having been invoked and asserts cr cells record and cr status agree with it.

tasks.title: Report every lens that never ran
tasks.acceptance:
- Every lens that did not run appears in the coverage report with its reason: a disabled axis, an unavailable axis, the unavailable reinvention half of §4.3.1, and a role skipped per §4.6.4, per §4.5.4.
- cr never reports a round as complete without stating all of them — a skipped role shrinks the cells §10.2.2 demands, so silence about it would let a complete verdict cover a lens that never looked.
- A test disables one axis, makes another unavailable, skips one role, and asserts all four reasons appear together with the completeness verdict.

tasks.title: Define the coverage cell fields
tasks.acceptance:
- Every cell carries the unit id and role id it sits at, one of pass, finding, question, or na, the head it was filled against, the unit hash of §3.4.6 it was filled for, and a reason when it is na, per §4.5.5.
- It also carries note_id when a note explained an unmapped unit per §4.1.5, and coverage with test_paths when the role is on the test axis per §4.4.1.
- A test asserts an na cell without a reason is rejected.

tasks.title: Store cells replacing named unit rows
tasks.acceptance:
- Cells are the agent's judgement and reach cr the same way findings do, through cr cells record <pr> <file.ndjson>, which replaces the current round's cell for each (unit, role) the file names and leaves every other cell untouched, per §4.5.6.
- cr rejects with exit code 1 a cell naming an unknown unit id or an inactive role.
- cr never invents a cell for a unit no role reported on — an unfilled cell is a coverage gap per §10.1.1, not something for cr to complete.
- A test records two of four cells and asserts the other two stay unfilled.

tasks.title: Compute cell head from owned state
tasks.acceptance:
- Round 8 finding agent-asserted-computed-field: head and the unit hash are computed on the cell. cr cells record stamps both from the current head and from units.ndjson for the named unit id, and rejects with exit code 1 a cell arriving carrying either — the same treatment §6.1.4 gives grade.
- Without this, §10.2.2's completeness check rests on a guard whose input is the very thing being guarded: an agent echoing the current hash makes a stale cell indistinguishable from a fresh one, and P6's coverage is proven reduces to coverage asserted.
- A test records a cell, re-clusters at a changed unit, and asserts the old cell fails §10.2.2's hash comparison automatically.

tasks.title: Reject a pass cell contradicting records
tasks.acceptance:
- Round 8 finding cell-record-consistency-unchecked: a (unit, role) carrying a pass cell for which the current round holds a record from that role on that unit is rejected with exit code 1, or reported by cr status, naming both. Without it a role can file a pass cell while recording a finding on the same unit in the same round, and cr status prints a complete row with a clean verdict.
- This direction admits no legitimate exception, because a waiver drop per §6.4.4 and a posted-index drop per §9.3.6 can only remove records, never create them.
- The opposite direction is left unenforced deliberately and the asymmetry is stated: a finding cell with no surviving record is the expected outcome of §6.4.4 and §9.3.6.
- A test files a pass cell alongside a record from the same role on the same unit and asserts the rejection.

tasks.title: Emit one prompt per role-unit cell
tasks.acceptance:
- cr review <pr> emits the prompts an agent runs. It performs no judgement of its own and calls no model, per §4.6.
- For every active role of §2.5 and every unit of §3.4, cr emits one prompt carrying the role's instructions and focus, the unit's hunks, the claims mapped to it, the candidate symbols of §4.3.1, the rule hits of §4.3.6, the test files of §4.4.1, and the threads and notes of §3.5.3 and §4.1.5, per §4.6.1.
- A test asserts all seven attachments appear in an emitted prompt.

tasks.title: State the output path with schema
tasks.acceptance:
- Every prompt names the NDJSON path the role writes to, and states the record schema of §6.1 together with the fields the agent may not write per §6.1.4, per §4.6.2.
- cr review never writes to findings.ndjson, per §4.6.3.
- A test asserts findings.ndjson is untouched by a review fan-out.

tasks.title: Report the cell set review expects
tasks.acceptance:
- cr review reports the set of cells it expects to be filled, so §10.2.2 can be checked once the roles return, per §4.6.3.
- The expected set is the cross product of active roles and units, minus nothing.
- A test compares the reported set against §10.2.2's demand for the same round.

tasks.title: Report skipped roles with their reasons
tasks.acceptance:
- A role whose prerequisites are unmet is reported as skipped with its reason, never omitted silently, per §4.6.4.
- The report feeds §4.5.4's honesty channel and survives --quiet.
- A test skips one role and asserts it appears in both cr review's output and cr status's lens list.

tasks.title: Run the intent axis in passes
tasks.acceptance:
- cr review runs in two passes. cr review <pr> --axis intent emits prompts carrying the units and the claims but no mapping; the intent role produces the mapping and the agent stores it with cr map record per §4.1.6, per §4.6.5.
- Once the mapping is stored, cr review <pr> --axis intent re-emits one prompt per unit mapped to zero claims, carrying the notes of §4.1.5, so §4.1.2 and §4.1.5 have an emitting pass — unmapped-ness is unknowable on the first.
- cr review <pr> refuses the remaining axes with exit code 4 until a mapping exists for the current round and head.
- A test drives both passes and asserts the second emits only zero-claim units.

tasks.title: Stamp mapping existence onto the metadata
tasks.acceptance:
- Round 9 finding mapping-existence-unobservable: cr map record stamps the round and head of the stored mapping on meta.json, and §4.6.5's gate reads that stamp rather than inferring existence from mapping.ndjson's record count.
- Without it a legitimately empty mapping — every unit mapped to zero claims, which happens whenever an issue key resolves but the agent extracts no claims — is byte-identical to a cleared or never-written file, and the pull request either unblocks wrongly or deadlocks permanently, since §4.6.6's escape hatch only covers an unavailable intent axis.
- A test records an empty mapping and asserts the remaining axes unblock; a second test asserts an absent mapping still exits 4.
- Round 12 finding empty-vs-absent-mapping, re-reported: the meta.json stamp above is what makes an empty mapping distinguishable from an absent one.

tasks.title: Skip mapping when intent is unavailable
tasks.acceptance:
- When the intent axis is unavailable per §4.5.3 there is no intent role and no mapping to produce. cr map record is then neither required nor accepted, the mapping is treated as empty, and §4.1.2 and §4.1.3 raise no items — an absent tracker is not an unmapped unit, per §4.6.6.
- A test drives a keyless PR through the full fan-out and asserts no unmapped-unit question and no intent-gap entry appears.

tasks.title: Create the sandbox worktree at head
tasks.acceptance:
- cr sandbox create <pr> creates a git worktree at the PR head under ~/.cr/state/<owner>/<repo>/pr-<n>/sandbox/, per §5.1.1.
